name: NY-12
label: Safe D

key_factors: Micah Lasher's large fundraising and outside spending advantage
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
Open seat after Jerry Nadler's retirement
model.rationale: The seat's +33 Democratic lean makes it out of reach for a Republican in a normal environment, and Lasher's $3.3 million raised plus $10.8 million in outside support dwarfs Shinkle's $155,000. Markets price a Democratic win near 97%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: A sharp national Republican wave or a major scandal involving Lasher could narrow the margin, though a flip remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jerry Nadler (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
This Manhattan-based seat is one of the most Democratic districts in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly +33. Jerry Nadler's retirement leaves an open seat, but the Democratic nominee Micah Lasher enters with overwhelming advantages: he has raised about $3.3 million and benefited from more than $10 million in outside spending, while Republican Caroline Shinkle has raised about $155,000 with no outside support.

No public polls cover the race, but prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 97%. Two minor independent candidates lack the resources to matter. The forecast expects Lasher to win by a wide, though not fully partisan-lean-sized, margin.
